questions.question: Which of the following are key advantages of Solid-State Drives (SSDs) compared to traditional mechanical hard drives? (Choose two)
options: A) Faster data access speeds
B) Lower cost per gigabyte of storage capacity
C) Resistance to physical shocks and drops
D) Reliance on rapid spinning magnetic metal platters
questions.explanation: SSDs feature no moving mechanical parts, providing drastically faster data access speeds and high resistance to physical shocks or drops compared to traditional mechanical hard drives[cite: 66].

questions.question: Which of the following RAID levels provide fault tolerance or redundancy? (Choose two)
options: A) RAID 0
B) RAID 1
C) RAID 5
D) RAID 10
questions.explanation: RAID 1 (mirroring/duplexing), RAID 5 (distributed parity), and RAID 10 (striped mirrors) all provide redundancy and fault tolerance, whereas RAID 0 offers zero redundancy[cite: 99, 101, 102, 104, 106].

questions.question: Which of the following storage interfaces connect internal magnetic hard drives (HDDs), solid-state drives (SSDs), and optical disc drives? (Choose two)
options: A) SATA
B) PATA
C) Serial ATA
D) Serial Port COM1
questions.explanation: SATA stands for Serial Advanced Technology Attachment (often referred to simply as Serial ATA) and is used to connect internal HDDs, SSDs, and optical disc drives[cite: 42].

questions.question: To interface completely with a computer system, a standard internal 2.5-inch or 3.5-inch SATA drive utilizes which two physical connections?
options: A) 7-pin data port
B) 15-pin power connector
C) 24-pin main motherboard power connector
D) 4-pin Berg connector
questions.explanation: A standard internal SATA drive utilizes a 7-pin data port to connect to the motherboard and a 15-pin power connector to connect to the power supply unit[cite: 43].

questions.question: Which of the following describe valid form factor widths for standard storage drives and media? (Choose two)
options: A) 2.5-inch
B) 3.5-inch
C) 4.0-inch
D) 10.0-inch
questions.explanation: Standard storage form factor widths include 2.5-inch (optimized for laptops and standard SATA SSDs) and 3.5-inch (the mechanical standard for desktop HDDs)[cite: 52, 60].

questions.question: What are the primary benefits of serial communication over legacy parallel buses in storage design? (Choose two)
options: A) Fewer physical I/O lines and narrower cables that improve internal airflow
B) Higher susceptibility to electromagnetic crosstalk
C) High resistance to signal degradation enabling longer distances
D) Requirement of dozens of parallel wires per data channel
questions.explanation: Serial communication requires far fewer I/O pins and wires, improves airflow, resists electromagnetic interference/crosstalk, and supports longer physical distances[cite: 41].

questions.question: Which of the following are valid spindle rotational speeds for mechanical hard drives? (Choose two)
options: A) 7,200 RPM
questions.explanation: Common consumer and enterprise mechanical HDD speeds include 5,400 RPM, 7,200 RPM, 10,000 RPM, and 15,000 RPM[cite: 53].

questions.question: Which of the following actions are recommended or required when handling external USB flash drives? (Choose two)
options: A) Always use the operating system's safe remove/eject utility before unplugging
B) Pull the drive out immediately while write-caching operations are active
C) Protect data integrity by avoiding premature disconnection
D) Run a full mechanical disk defragmentation utility on the flash drive monthly
questions.explanation: Users and technicians must always use the OS safe remove/eject utility before unplugging external USB drives to protect data integrity and avoid corrupting write-cached background operations[cite: 87].

questions.question: Which of the following statements regarding Solid-State Hybrid Drives (SSHDs) are correct? (Choose two)
options: A) They combine a traditional mechanical HDD with a built-in solid-state flash memory cache.
B) An internal controller automatically caches frequently accessed files into flash memory.
C) They rely entirely on flash memory chips with zero mechanical platters.
D) They require manual user intervention to move files into the flash cache.
questions.explanation: SSHDs combine a mechanical hard disk drive with a small flash memory cache, and an internal controller automatically monitors and copies frequently accessed files into the fast cache[cite: 79, 80].

questions.question: Which of the following statements about NVMe (Non-Volatile Memory Express) are true? (Choose two)
options: A) It is an ultra-low latency protocol designed for non-volatile flash storage.
B) It is bottlenecked by legacy SATA controller limits of 600 MB/s.
C) It connects directly to the system's PCI Express (PCIe) bus.
D) It requires a 15-pin SATA power connector to operate.
questions.explanation: NVMe is an ultra-low latency storage communication protocol designed for flash storage that connects directly to the PCIe bus, bypassing legacy SATA bottlenecks[cite: 76, 77].

questions.question: Which of the following characteristics apply to RAID 0? (Choose two)
options: A) Requires a minimum of two drives
B) Provides high performance through disk striping
C) Provides built-in data redundancy and fault tolerance
D) Automatically rebuilds lost data if a disk fails
questions.explanation: RAID 0 requires at least two drives, splits file blocks across disks for high performance, but offers zero redundancy[cite: 99].

questions.question: Which of the following are true regarding SD card specifications and standards? (Choose two)
options: A) SDXC stands for SD eXtended Capacity and supports up to 2 TB.
B) Standard SD cards measure 32 mm x 24 mm.
C) microSD cards are larger than standard SD cards.
D) SD cards cannot be write-protected under any circumstances.
questions.explanation: SDXC supports up to 2 TB capacity, and standard SD cards have physical dimensions of 32 mm x 24 mm[cite: 120, 121].

questions.question: Which of the following are valid guidelines when implementing a hardware RAID array? (Choose two)
options: A) Build arrays using identical drives (same capacity, model, and speed) for optimal performance.
B) If mixed capacities are used, the controller truncates larger drives to match the smallest disk.
C) RAID arrays completely eliminate the need for external backups.
D) Hardware RAID is always managed directly by the operating system software.
questions.explanation: Optimal performance requires matching drives, and mixing capacities causes the RAID controller to truncate larger drives down to the smallest disk size[cite: 95].

questions.question: What are the primary functions of the TRIM command and SSD maintenance practices? (Choose two)
options: A) TRIM tells the SSD controller which deleted data blocks are no longer needed for background wiping.
B) Traditional defragmentation utilities should never be run on SSDs because they cause unnecessary write wear.
C) Defragmentation should be run daily on SSDs to maximize flash cell lifespan.
D) TRIM forces the SSD to convert back into magnetic mechanical platters.
questions.explanation: TRIM lets the SSD wipe deleted blocks in the background, and running traditional defrag on an SSD causes unnecessary write wear without performance benefit[cite: 73, 75].

questions.question: Which of the following are physical internal geometry terms associated with mechanical Hard Disk Drives? (Choose two)
options: A) Platter
B) Spindle
C) Flash cell block
D) TRIM controller
questions.explanation: Platters (magnetic circular disks) and spindles (central axis motor holding/spinning platters) are core physical geometry components of mechanical HDDs[cite: 55, 56].

questions.question: Which SATA standard revisions correspond to the correct maximum data transfer rates? (Choose two)
options: A) SATA Revision 3.0 supports 6 Gb/s (600 MB/s)
B) SATA Revision 3.2 supports 16 Gb/s (1969 MB/s)
C) SATA Revision 3.0 supports 16 Gb/s
D) SATA Revision 3.2 supports 1.5 Gb/s
questions.explanation: SATA Revision 3.0 specifies 6 Gb/s (600 MB/s), while SATA Revision 3.2 reaches 16 Gb/s (1969 MB/s) by leveraging PCIe bus signaling[cite: 48, 49].

questions.question: Which of the following describe features of RAID 5? (Choose two)
options: A) Requires a minimum of 3 drives
B) Distributes data and parity information across all drives
C) Requires a minimum of 2 drives with no parity
D) Cannot sustain any drive failures without total data loss
questions.explanation: RAID 5 requires a minimum of 3 drives and distributes both data and parity across all disks in the array[cite: 102].

questions.question: What steps are involved when configuring hardware RAID before installing an operating system? (Choose two)
options: A) Enable the storage controller and change mode from AHCI to RAID in BIOS/UEFI
B) Reboot and press the manufacturer hotkey combination to enter the RAID configuration utility
C) Format all drives to FAT16 from within Windows Device Manager
D) Disconnect all SATA cables from the motherboard permanently
questions.explanation: Configuring hardware RAID requires changing the SATA mode to RAID in BIOS/UEFI and using the controller hotkey utility during startup to define the array[cite: 108, 110].

questions.question: Which of the following are common SSD form factors? (Choose two)
options: A) 2.5-inch SATA
B) M.2
C) 5.25-inch optical tray
D) PATA ribbon card
questions.explanation: Common SSD form factors include 2.5-inch SATA drives and slim M.2 expansion cards[cite: 67, 69].

questions.question: Which of the following statements about file recovery and management on storage drives are accurate? (Choose two)
options: A) Accidentally deleted files can often be restored directly from the Recycle Bin.
B) If files bypass the Recycle Bin, technicians can deploy specialized third-party data recovery software to search unallocated space.
C) Windows built-in GUI tools can always recover permanently wiped sectors on damaged flash chips.
D) Formatting a drive restores permanently deleted files instantly without software.
questions.explanation: Standard recovery involves checking the Recycle Bin or using specialized third-party data recovery software to search unallocated drive space if the bin was bypassed[cite: 65].

questions.question: Which of the following describe RAID 10 (RAID 1+0)? (Choose two)
options: A) It is a nested RAID level often described as a "stripe of mirrors".
B) It requires a minimum of four physical drives.
C) It provides zero redundancy and high failure vulnerability.
D) It distributes single parity blocks across two disks.
questions.explanation: RAID 10 is a nested configuration combining striping and mirroring ('stripe of mirrors') requiring a minimum of four drives[cite: 104].

questions.question: What are the characteristics of flash memory media? (Choose two)
options: A) Non-volatile electronic storage that retains data without power
B) Solid-state technology that can be electronically erased and reprogrammed
C) Volatile memory that requires constant electricity like RAM
D) Magnetic storage relying on spinning metal platters
questions.explanation: Flash memory is solid-state, non-volatile electronic storage that retains data securely without requiring a constant power source[cite: 114].

questions.question: Which of the following are true regarding mechanical hard drive geometry and structure? (Choose two)
options: A) Actuator arms move read/write heads across spinning platters.
B) Tracks, sectors, and cylinders define the physical layout of data on platters.
C) Hard drives utilize laser diodes to read pits and lands on optical polycarbonate layers.
D) Mechanical drives store data exclusively in electronic flash cells.
questions.explanation: Mechanical hard drives use actuator arms with read/write heads moving across platters organized into tracks, sectors, and cylinders[cite: 57, 58].

questions.question: Which of the following interfaces support native hot-swapping in mainstream operating systems? (Choose two)
options: A) USB
B) eSATA
C) Legacy PATA ribbon cables
D) Internal motherboard parallel printer ports
questions.explanation: Modern mainstream operating systems natively support hot-swapping for USB drives and eSATA external enclosures[cite: 83].

questions.question: What is the distinction between disk and disc terminology according to CompTIA guidelines? (Choose two)
options: A) "Disk" refers to magnetic media storage such as an HDD.
B) "Disc" refers to optical media storage such as CDs, DVDs, and Blu-Ray.
C) "Disk" and "disc" are completely interchangeable terms with no technical distinction.
D) "Disc" refers exclusively to solid-state flash memory chips.
questions.explanation: CompTIA specifies that 'disk' refers to magnetic media (HDD) while 'disc' refers to optical media (CD, DVD, Blu-Ray)[cite: 59].

questions.question: Which of the following are valid SD card capacity classifications? (Choose two)
options: A) SDHC (SD High Capacity)
B) SDXC (SD eXtended Capacity)
C) SDVC (SD Video Capacity)
D) SDRAM (SD Random Access Memory)
questions.explanation: SD card capacity standards include SDHC (High Capacity) and SDXC (eXtended Capacity)[cite: 121].

questions.question: Which of the following factors explain why higher spindle rotational speeds improve mechanical HDD performance? (Choose two)
options: A) They drastically reduce rotational latency.
B) They help the read/write head reach target sectors on platters faster.
C) They convert magnetic storage into electronic flash memory.
D) They eliminate the need for actuator arms.
questions.explanation: Higher RPM speeds reduce rotational latency, which is the physical delay in time it takes for the drive head to reach a specific target sector[cite: 53, 54].

questions.question: Which of the following statements about RAID redundancy and backups are correct? (Choose two)
options: A) RAID IS NOT A BACKUP SOLUTION.
B) RAID protects against immediate physical drive hardware failures.
C) RAID protects against malware infection, file corruption, and accidental file deletion.
D) RAID eliminates the need for any disaster recovery planning.
questions.explanation: RAID guards only against immediate physical drive failures and is not a backup solution against file corruption, malware, or accidental deletions[cite: 92].

questions.question: Which of the following describe software-based RAID versus hardware-based RAID? (Choose two)
options: A) Software RAID is managed directly by the computer's operating system.
B) Hardware RAID is managed by a dedicated controller card or chipset.
C) Software RAID requires specialized PCIe controller cards with dedicated processors.
D) Hardware RAID consumes host CPU resources to calculate parity.
questions.explanation: Software-based RAID is managed by the OS using system resources, whereas hardware-based RAID uses a dedicated controller card or chipset independently[cite: 93].

questions.question: What are the primary roles of USB flash drives in IT environments? (Choose two)
options: A) Quick data transfer between systems
B) Booting systems for operating system installation purposes
C) Long-term archival storage of enterprise databases
D) Acting as internal RAID 5 parity controllers
questions.explanation: USB flash drives are quick, efficient tools meant for transferring data and booting systems for installation, not for long-term storage[cite: 118].

questions.question: Which of the following are true regarding mechanical hard drive fragmentation? (Choose two)
options: A) It occurs when individual files are broken into pieces and stored in non-contiguous clusters.
B) It slows down system performance during hard drive reads and writes.
C) It benefits SSDs by cleaning up flash memory blocks.
D) It is caused by running the TRIM command too often.
questions.explanation: Fragmentation happens when file pieces are stored across non-contiguous clusters, which slows down system performance during reads and writes[cite: 63].

questions.question: Which of the following describe NVMe architectural advantages over SATA SSDs? (Choose two)
options: A) Bypasses legacy SATA controller limits of 600 MB/s
B) Connects directly to the high-speed PCIe bus
C) Relies on mechanical platters to reduce manufacturing costs
D) Mandates the use of PATA ribbon cables
questions.explanation: NVMe overcomes the 600 MB/s SATA bottleneck by connecting directly to the high-speed PCIe bus[cite: 77].

questions.question: What are the benefits of using a Solid-State Hybrid Drive (SSHD)? (Choose two)
options: A) Near-SSD boot speeds and responsiveness for core files
B) Massive traditional mechanical storage capacity at a cost-effective price point
C) Complete elimination of mechanical components
D) Requiring no internal controller logic
questions.explanation: SSHDs offer a middle-ground compromise providing near-SSD boot speeds alongside the cheap, massive capacity of a traditional hard drive[cite: 81].

questions.question: Which of the following are valid SD card physical size classifications? (Choose two)
options: A) Standard SD
B) microSD
C) megaSD
D) ultraSD
questions.explanation: Valid SD card sizes include Standard SD, miniSD, and microSD[cite: 120].

questions.question: Which of the following statements about RAID 1 are correct? (Choose two)
options: A) It performs disk mirroring or duplexing.
B) It requires a minimum of two hard drives.
C) It stripes data across four drives with distributed parity.
D) It provides zero redundancy.
questions.explanation: RAID 1 involves mirroring or duplexing across at least two hard drives for high redundancy[cite: 101, 106].

questions.question: What are the roles of parity bits and error checking in data storage? (Choose two)
options: A) Parity is an extra bit that indicates whether information is missing or corrupted.
B) Parity helps determine if data bits sum to odd or even totals.
C) Parity doubles the physical storage capacity of an SSD.
D) Parity replaces the need for a file system.
questions.explanation: A parity bit tells the computer if information is missing by checking if data bit sums are odd (parity 1) or even (parity 0)[cite: 88].

questions.question: Which of the following steps are part of installing a desktop 2.5-inch SSD? (Choose two)
options: A) Mount the SSD into an adapter bracket and secure it into a spare drive bay.
B) Attach the SATA data cable from the SSD to the motherboard and connect power from the PSU.
C) Run low-level magnetic formatting on the platters.
D) Solder the SSD pins directly to the CPU socket.
questions.explanation: Desktop 2.5-inch SSD installation involves mounting the drive in an adapter bracket within a bay, then connecting the SATA data cable and power connector[cite: 71].

questions.question: Which of the following describe enterprise storage server practices? (Choose two)
options: A) Utilizing hot-swappable internal SATA and SAS bays
B) Replacing failed storage disks on the fly without system downtime
C) Shutting down the entire data center to replace a single failed drive
D) Relying exclusively on unformatted USB flash drives for core virtualization
questions.explanation: Enterprise storage servers use hot-swappable internal SATA and SAS bays to replace failed disks on the fly without causing downtime[cite: 84].

questions.question: Which of the following are true about SSD flash memory behavior? (Choose two)
options: A) Flash cells cannot overwrite data directly and must erase entire blocks before writing new data.
B) Automated TRIM commands help wipe deleted blocks clean in the background.
C) SSDs suffer severe performance degradation from file fragmentation across physical chips.
D) SSDs require mechanical read heads to locate sectors on flash chips.
questions.explanation: SSD flash cells cannot overwrite directly and require block erasure; TRIM assists by clearing deleted blocks in the background to maintain full write speed[cite: 74, 75].

questions.question: Which of the following are valid characteristics of serial communication? (Choose two)
options: A) Sends one bit at a time
B) Sends data in the form of binary voltage pulses
C) Sends entire bytes simultaneously across 8 or more parallel wires
D) Requires high-voltage multi-pin parallel ribbon cables
questions.explanation: Serial communication sends one bit at a time using fewer I/O lines via binary voltage pulses (high/low states)[cite: 40].

questions.question: What are the primary functions of SD card speed class ratings? (Choose two)
options: A) Indicating minimum sustained write speeds, such as V30 for 30 MB/s
B) Helping users choose cards capable of handling sustained video recording
C) Measuring the exact physical weight of the card in grams
D) Determining the motherboard CPU socket compatibility
questions.explanation: SD cards are labeled with video speed class ratings (e.g., V30) to indicate minimum write speeds required for reliable video recording[cite: 122].

questions.question: Which of the following describe potential consequences of pulling out an external USB drive without using the OS eject utility? (Choose two)
options: A) Severe data corruption
B) Breaking the drive's file system completely
C) Automatically upgrading the USB controller firmware
D) Formatting the drive into an optimized RAID 5 array
questions.explanation: Pulling an external drive out before cached background write operations finish can easily cause severe data corruption or break the file system[cite: 87].

questions.question: Which of the following are true regarding M.2 and PCIe storage solutions? (Choose two)
options: A) M.2 is a slim, rectangular expansion card form factor mounting flat on motherboards.
B) PCIe expansion cards plug directly into motherboard slots for high-speed storage.
C) M.2 drives require traditional 5.25-inch optical drive bays.
D) PCIe storage cards operate exclusively via legacy PATA controllers.
questions.explanation: M.2 drives mount flat on supported motherboards, and PCIe expansion cards plug directly into motherboard slots for high-speed storage[cite: 69, 70].

questions.question: Which RAID levels require a minimum of four hard drives? (Choose two)
options: A) RAID 10 (RAID 1+0)
B) RAID 0 (under specific multi-channel controller configurations)
C) RAID 1
D) RAID 5
questions.explanation: RAID 10 strictly requires a minimum of four drives[cite: 104, 106], and striped array setups like RAID 0 can utilize four or more drives.

questions.question: Which of the following are valid characteristics of eSATA storage connections? (Choose two)
options: A) Provides external SATA connectivity
B) Features shielded cabling ports designed for external enclosures
C) Operates exclusively inside sealed hard drive chassis
D) Replaces internal power supplies with optical lasers
questions.explanation: eSATA provides external SATA connectivity using specialized shielded cabling ports for external enclosures[cite: 83].

questions.question: Which of the following statements about disk fragmentation maintenance tools are true? (Choose two)
options: A) Windows utilities like Disk Defragmenter and Optimize Drives help rearrange fragmented files on HDDs.
B) Running defragmentation utilities on mechanical HDDs improves read and write efficiency.
C) Defragmentation tools should be run on SSDs daily to clear flash cells.
D) Defragmentation tools convert mechanical HDDs into solid-state hybrid drives.
questions.explanation: Programs like Disk Defragmenter and Optimize Drives rearrange files on mechanical HDDs to improve read/write efficiency[cite: 63].

questions.question: Which of the following describe potential drive failure tolerances across different RAID levels? (Choose two)
options: A) RAID 1 can sustain the failure of 1 drive.
B) RAID 5 can sustain the failure of 1 drive.
C) RAID 0 can sustain the failure of up to 2 drives without data loss.
D) RAID 1 can sustain zero failures.
questions.explanation: Both RAID 1 and RAID 5 can sustain 1 functional drive failure without losing data[cite: 106].

questions.question: Which of the following are true regarding mSATA storage devices? (Choose two)
options: A) It is a legacy, miniaturized form factor card.
B) It was commonly used in older thin laptops.
C) It is identical in physical dimensions to a 3.5-inch desktop HDD.
D) It connects exclusively via 5.25-inch optical ribbon cables.
questions.explanation: mSATA is a legacy, miniaturized form factor card used in older thin laptops[cite: 68].

questions.question: Which of the following actions correctly prepare a system for building a hardware RAID array in BIOS/UEFI? (Choose two)
options: A) Ensure target hard drives are securely connected to motherboard SATA RAID storage ports.
B) Change the onboard storage interface mode from standard AHCI to RAID.
C) Set the system boot order to 3.5-inch floppy disks only.
D) Disable all motherboard storage controllers permanently.
questions.explanation: Setting up hardware RAID requires verifying drive connections to RAID ports and changing the storage mode from AHCI to RAID in BIOS/UEFI[cite: 107, 108].
